children: Jin Air could benefit from a planned merger next year, Hana Securities analyst Dohyun Ahn says. The South Korean low-cost carrier and two local peers, Air Busan and Air Seoul, are scheduled to merge under the Jin Air brand in March 2027, as their parents, Korean Air Lines and Asiana Airlines, continue integrating operations. Ahn expects Jin Air to become South Korea's largest premium low-cost carrier and improve profitability by streamlining overlapping routes and services. Lower jet-fuel prices and robust demand for budget air travel could also provide favorable operating environments, she adds. Hana expects Jin Air's operating profit to reach 177 billion won in 2027 and 258 billion won in 2028, with its operating profit margin widening to 8.5% from 5.8% over the same period. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
